problems.title: A difference of two squares
problems.question: Calculate 199²−1.
problems.idea: Use the neighbouring factors instead of squaring directly.

problems.title: Propagate a remainder through a linear expression
problems.question: a has remainder 3 on division by 11. Find the remainder of 2a+7 on division by 11.
problems.idea: Replace a by 11k+3.
steps: The remainder is 2.

problems.title: A reciprocal ratio
problems.question: a is 25% larger than b. How many times is 1/b as large as 1/a?
problems.idea: Divide the two reciprocals in the requested order.
steps: Thus the factor is 5/4.

problems.title: Two midpoint area reductions
problems.question: D is midpoint of BC and E of AC in triangle ABC. Area ABE=36. Find area BDE.
problems.idea: A median halves area; then use the midpoint base BC.
formulas: Area ABE=area ABC/2; distance from E to BC=half the distance from A.
steps: Area ABC=72.
Triangle BDE has half the BC base and half the altitude, so its area is 72/4.

problems.title: A median to the hypotenuse
problems.question: In right triangle ABC, AB is the hypotenuse and CO its median. CO=CB=5. Find AC.
problems.idea: The hypotenuse median equals half the hypotenuse.

problems.title: The next integer above a cube root
problems.question: Find the smallest positive integer larger than ∛65.
problems.idea: Compare 65 with nearby integer cubes.

problems.title: A number divisible by both 15 and 20
problems.question: Which listed number must divide a positive integer divisible by 15 and 20?
problems.idea: It must be divisible by their least common multiple.
steps: Therefore 60 always divides the integer. The other listed divisors need not.

problems.title: Combine fractions from differently sized plots
problems.question: Two plots have area ratio 3:5. Apples cover 2/3 of the first and 3/5 of the second. What fraction of the combined area is planted?
problems.idea: Use areas 3t and 5t.
steps: The total area is 8t, so the fraction is 5t/(8t).

problems.title: A missing coefficient in the choices
problems.question: If a−b=1, express a³−b³ in terms of b.
problems.idea: Substitute a=b+1 and expand.
steps: The b³ terms cancel, leaving the two quadratic and linear contributions and 1.
problems.note: The printed choice 1+3b+b² omits the coefficient 3 on b²; none of the choices is the correct general identity.

problems.title: Reflection across the horizontal axis
problems.question: Which graph is the reflection of y=3(x−1)²+2 across the x-axis?
problems.idea: Negate the whole output.
steps: The answer is −3(x−1)²−2.

problems.title: Compare coefficients in a factorization
problems.question: x²−5x+k=(x−1)(x−c). Find k.
problems.idea: Expand the right side.
steps: Matching x-coefficients gives c+1=5, so c=4.
The constant term is k=c.

problems.title: Two trains meeting between stations
problems.question: Two trains leave stations 80 km apart and meet after t hours. One travels at v km/h. Find the second speed, assuming they move toward each other.
problems.idea: Their distances travelled add to 80.
steps: Solve for u: u=80/t−v.

problems.title: Parallelism statements about lines and planes
problems.question: Which of the three printed statements is always true: planes parallel to the same line are parallel; planes parallel to the same plane are parallel; lines parallel to the same plane are parallel?
problems.idea: Only equal plane-normal directions force plane parallelism.
formulas: If α∥γ and β∥γ, their normal vectors are parallel, so α∥β for distinct α,β.
steps: The first statement fails for two intersecting vertical planes both parallel to a vertical line located off them.
The third fails for nonparallel lines in a plane parallel to the given plane.

problems.title: A vector length missing from the choices
problems.question: Given AC=(2,6) and BC=(1,2), find |AB|.
problems.idea: Subtract the two vectors ending at C.
steps: Its length is √(1²+4²)=√17.
problems.note: None of the printed integers 4,5,6,7 equals √17.

problems.title: Square roots of squares require absolute values
problems.question: Evaluate √[(1−2cos45°)²]−√[(1+2sin45°)²].
problems.idea: Use √u²=|u|.
steps: The first absolute value is |1−√2|=√2−1.
The second is 1+√2. Their difference is −2.

problems.title: A square diagonal divided by a midpoint line
problems.question: Square ABCD has side 2. E is midpoint of BC; DE meets AC at F. Find AF.
problems.idea: Use coordinates to find the fraction of the diagonal.
steps: Their intersection is F=(4/3,4/3).
problems.note: The listed 4/3 is a coordinate of F, not the length AF. The length needs the factor √2.

problems.title: Identify an odd function
problems.question: Which listed function is odd: ln x, x²−5, x³+x, or 1/(x+3)?
problems.idea: Check both domain symmetry and f(−x)=−f(x).
steps: The polynomial’s domain is symmetric and the required equality holds for every x.

problems.title: A logarithmic inequality with an argument restriction
problems.question: Solve log₈(x²−4x+3)≤1.
problems.idea: Base 8 is increasing, so the argument must lie in (0,8].
formulas: x²−4x+3>0 gives x<1 or x>3; x²−4x+3≤8 gives −1≤x≤5.
steps: Intersect the two conditions and retain the closed endpoints where the log equals 1.

problems.title: Two rays in a regular octagon
problems.question: In regular octagon ABCDEFGH, rays DB and FA meet at P. Find angle APB.
problems.idea: Use coordinates on the unit circumcircle.
steps: DB is horizontal. Extending FA to height 1/√2 gives P=(2+1/√2,1/√2).
At P, PB points horizontally left. The downward-left vector PA has vertical/horizontal magnitude ratio (1/√2)/(1+1/√2)=√2−1.
This is tan22.5°.

problems.title: A side ratio with an obtuse included angle
problems.question: AB=28, angle C=120°, AC:BC=3:5. Find the smallest side.
problems.idea: Use the cosine rule with AC=3t,BC=5t.
steps: The right side is 49t², so t=4.
The side lengths are 12,20,28; the smallest is 12.

problems.title: Area of a regular dodecagon
problems.question: A regular dodecagon has circumradius 2. Find its area.
problems.idea: Split it into 12 congruent central triangles.

problems.title: A homothety centred at the origin
problems.question: A dilation of factor k maps (2,3) to (2x−1,x). Find k.
problems.idea: Both coordinates must be multiplied by k.
steps: Substitute x=3k into the first: 2k=6k−1.
Thus 4k=1.

problems.title: A bisected obtuse angle in an isosceles trapezoid
problems.question: An isosceles trapezoid has bases 3 and 5, and a diagonal bisects an obtuse angle. Find its area.
problems.idea: Parallel bases create an isosceles triangle using the larger base and a leg.
formulas: The diagonal-bisector equality and alternate angles force leg length=larger base=5.
steps: Half the base difference is 1. The height is √(5²−1²)=2√6.
The area is midline·height=((3+5)/2)·2√6.

problems.title: A chord parallel to a tangent
problems.question: AB,AC are tangents from A to a circle at B,C. Chord CD is parallel to AB and angle BAC=40°. Find angle DBC.
problems.idea: Use the central angle between the two tangency radii.
steps: By the tangent-chord theorem and CD∥AB, the two angles at C and D in triangle BCD are 70° each.
The remaining angle at B is 180°−140°.

problems.title: A side sum and the sine rule
problems.question: In triangle ABC, A=30°,B=45°, and AC+BC=18(1+√2). Find BC.
problems.idea: The sine rule gives the ratio of the two sides.
steps: Thus AC=√2·BC and the given sum is BC(1+√2).
Divide by 1+√2.

problems.title: A parallelogram side from its diagonals
problems.question: A parallelogram has diagonals 10 and 12 with angle 30°. Find its longer side.
problems.idea: A side is half the sum or difference of the diagonal vectors.

problems.title: Only the central gaps are shaded
problems.question: Two unit circles touch each other and the sides of a 4-by-2 rectangle. Find the shaded central region in the diagram.
problems.idea: The diagram shades two central gaps, leaving the four outer corner gaps unshaded.
steps: Vertical symmetry through each circle centre pairs the shaded central gaps with the unshaded outer gaps. Their areas are equal.
Therefore the shaded area is half of 8−2π.

problems.title: Ratios of arithmetic-progression terms
problems.question: A positive arithmetic progression has fifth term three times its second. How many times is its seventh term as large as its third?
problems.idea: Write every term using first term a and difference d.
steps: This gives d=2a.
The seventh term is a+6d=13a; the third is a+2d=5a.
Their ratio is 13/5.

problems.title: A median fixes one of three nonlinear data values
problems.question: The nonnegative data are x,x²,1, with median 1/4. Find their mean.
problems.idea: Determine the ordering from x.
steps: In both possible orders the median is x, so x=1/4.

problems.title: Pie-chart angles reveal a class size
problems.question: The first class has one more boy and one fewer girl than the second. The second girls’ pie-chart sector is 30° larger. How many pupils are in the first class?
problems.idea: The two total class sizes are equal.
formulas: If total size is N, one pupil changes a sector by 360°/N.
steps: The girls’ counts differ by one, so 360°/N=30°.
Thus N=12.

problems.title: Intersect two linear inequalities
problems.question: Solve 3x−5≤−2x+11 and x+7>−3x.
problems.idea: Solve the inequalities separately, then intersect.
steps: The first gives x≤16/5, the second x>−7/4.

problems.title: Three consecutive geometric-progression terms
problems.question: Find x such that x,x+1,x+3 form a geometric progression in that order.
problems.idea: The middle term squared equals the product of the outer terms.
steps: Expansion gives x²+2x+1=x²+3x, so x=1.
The terms 1,2,4 indeed have common ratio 2.

problems.title: Two marked lengths on a hypotenuse
problems.question: In a right triangle with hypotenuse AB=16 and A=60°, points P,Q on AB satisfy AP=AC and BQ=BC. Find PQ.
problems.idea: Compute the legs and locate both points from A.
steps: AP=8 and AQ=16−8√3.

problems.title: A trapezoid with perpendicular diagonals
problems.question: An isosceles trapezoid has base ratio 2:3 and perpendicular diagonals. Find the cosine of its acute angle.
problems.idea: Use the horizontal runs of a leg and a diagonal.
formulas: Let bases 2t,3t; leg run=t/2; diagonal run=5t/2.
steps: The diagonals have opposite slopes. Perpendicularity forces height h=5t/2.
The leg length is √[(t/2)²+(5t/2)²]=t√26/2.
The acute-angle cosine is horizontal run divided by leg.

problems.title: An oblique segment and orthogonal projections
problems.question: AB,AC are equal oblique segments to a plane, with acute angle BAC=α. Their projections are perpendicular. Find the cosine of AB’s inclination to the plane.
problems.idea: The dot product of the oblique vectors consists only of the shared normal components.
formulas: Let segment length L and common height h. Then L²cosα=h².
steps: If inclination is θ, sinθ=h/L=√cosα.
Thus cosθ=√(1−cosα), positive for an acute inclination.

problems.title: Place 1 strictly between two quadratic roots
problems.question: For which a does 4x²−2x+a=0 have one root below 1 and one above 1?
problems.idea: An upward quadratic is negative strictly between its roots.
steps: The necessary and sufficient condition is f(1)<0. It also guarantees two distinct real roots.

problems.title: All sine roots in an open interval
problems.question: Find all roots of sin6x=√3/2 in (0,π/2).
problems.idea: First solve in the expanded interval 0<6x<3π.
steps: The allowed angle values are π/3,2π/3,7π/3,8π/3.
Divide each by 6.

problems.title: Three diameter circles and a shaded crescent
problems.question: Circles have diameters equal to the hypotenuse and legs of a right triangle with legs 1 and √3 cm. Find the shaded part of the hypotenuse circle outside both leg circles, as shown.
problems.idea: Use circular segments and add back the overlap counted twice.
formulas: Hypotenuse=2, so large radius=1; leg-circle radii=1/2,√3/2; segment area=r²(θ−sinθ)/2, with θ in radians.
steps: The overlap of the large circle with the √3-leg circle is its half-disk 3π/8 plus the large circle’s 120° segment π/3−√3/4: total 17π/24−√3/4.
The overlap with the unit-leg circle is its half-disk π/8 plus the large circle’s 60° segment π/6−√3/4: total 7π/24−√3/4.
The two leg circles overlap in a lens lying inside the large circle. Its two sectors have angles 60° and 120° and radii √3/2 and 1/2. The lens area is π/8+π/12−√3/4=5π/24−√3/4.
By inclusion-exclusion, shaded area=π−(17π/24−√3/4)−(7π/24−√3/4)+(5π/24−√3/4).
Simplify to 5π/24+√3/4.

problems.title: A larger purchase at a lower unit price
problems.question: A firm planned to spend 2000 lari. It bought 200 kg more than planned at 3 lari less per kg and spent 4000 lari. Find the actual price per kg.
problems.idea: Use actual price p>0; the planned price was p+3.
steps: Multiply and simplify to p²−7p−60=(p−12)(p+5)=0.
Only the positive root is a valid price.

problems.title: When a line lies strictly below a parabola
problems.question: Find a such that y≥x²−ax+2a−5 and y≤ax−13 have no common solution.
problems.idea: At any permitted x, the lower curve must not exceed the upper line.
steps: Complete the square: (x−a)²+9−(a−1)²≤0.
There is no solution exactly when the minimum 9−(a−1)² is strictly positive.
Thus |a−1|<3. At the endpoints the curves touch and one solution exists, so exclude them.
